## Goal
Turn the CUDApp research review into measured improvements to native model execution. Reuse existing code, qualification work and ownership. This roadmap adds research work; it does not replace the existing integration priorities.

Review baseline: 232332422bfdc31c8918085b50f13c1e18ab702e (2026-10-22).
Literature: [Undermind ranked research and papers](https://app.undermind.ai/projects/71b4b2d1-0818-4a84-8c00-452e1071922a?path=/CUDApp%20native%20GPU%20runtime%20research).

## Existing work to finish and reuse
Canonical motor integration #5 remains the priority. Reuse concurrency/recovery #6/#11/#12, general math #9, disassembler #10, repeatability #13, allocation guard #8 and overhead measurement #14. Preserve Omega PRs aien-dev/omega-mv#614 through #618 and carry their changes into the canonical backend without losing work during extraction. Recheck their live state before editing; do not recreate implementations that already exist.

Independent driver qualification #7 remains its own coordinated workstream. Native-runtime optimization experiments do not require a driver replacement and must not switch the live driver.

## Delivery sequence
1. Inspect current branches, instructions, source pins and active ownership. Establish the canonical integrated candidate under #5; complete the existing qualification sequence with the current owners.
2. Establish reproducible tests, numerical contracts and baseline measurement: #15, #16, #17.
3. Make targeted experiments: #18 MoE fusion, #20 shared-prefix attention, #22 SASS scheduling. Use #19 dependency analysis and #21 ragged planning where the measured bottleneck justifies them.
4. Evaluate #23 prefill traversal and #24/#25 memory ownership/import work under their explicit prerequisites.
5. Requalify successful integrations on the final source pins; update consumer pins and report end-to-end results. A reproducible negative experiment is useful evidence; never force an unsupported optimization into the default path.

## Work and dependencies
| Issue | Deliverable | Prerequisites for integration/performance claims |
|---|---|---|
| #15 | Reproducible host tests and pinned Omega slice harness | Reuse existing gates; host work may start immediately |
| #16 | Numerical contracts and end-to-end correctness | #5, existing #9/#13 references |
| #17 | Native model/launch/traffic benchmark report | #5, #16; reuse #14 accounting |
| #18 | FP8 gate/up + SwiGLU fusion experiment | #16, #17 |
| #19 | Buffer dependencies and narrower synchronization | #6, #16, #17 |
| #20 | Shared-prefix attention and stable state merge | #16, #17; existing paging/GQA |
| #21 | Ragged attention plan/run and bounded workspace | #16, #17; existing reservations |
| #22 | Bounded SASS schedule search and byte validation | #10, #16, #17 |
| #23 | Alternating prefill KV traversal experiment | #16, #17 |
| #24 | Coordinated memory reservations and ownership | #6, #8; reuse #14 |
| #25 | File-backed native weight mapping experiment | #6, #24, #16, #17 |

## Checklist
- [ ] #15 — Make host tests and Omega slice qualification reproducible from a fresh checkout
- [ ] #16 — Define numerical contracts for native kernels and whole-token decode
- [ ] #17 — Add a native benchmark report for token latency, launch costs and memory traffic
- [ ] #18 — Experiment: fuse FP8 gate/up and SwiGLU in the routed MoE decode path
- [ ] #19 — Add explicit buffer dependencies and validate narrower command-list synchronization
- [ ] #20 — Add shared-prefix attention execution with stable prefix/suffix state merging
- [ ] #21 — Separate ragged-attention planning from execution with bounded reusable workspaces
- [ ] #22 — Build bounded SASS schedule search with independent encoded-code validation
- [ ] #23 — Experiment: alternate KV traversal in GB10 prefill attention to improve cache reuse
- [ ] #24 — Extend memory admission with coordinated reservations and explicit buffer ownership
- [ ] #25 — Experiment: qualify file-backed shared weights through native GPU mappings

## Completion
Each child has its own acceptance and evidence gate. Track implementation, host/simulator qualification, GB10 qualification and consumer integration separately. Store source/binary/model/config identities and raw paired measurements; no performance promises copied from other GPUs. Preserve the baseline path until the candidate is qualified. No production restart, module unload, default-driver change or unsafe memory exhaustion through this roadmap.

Close the roadmap only when every child has an explicit evidenced outcome and the accepted changes pass the final integrated consumer workload, including golden/numerical checks, concurrent requests, a second turn and a real tool-call parse. Mark unavailable hardware work BLOCKED/NOT_RUN with its exact remaining gate instead of presenting it as complete.

## Direction

Finish integration and qualification of the existing GPU backend before adding another math operation. This is not an architectural redesign. Ledger L456 records Drake's revised order; implementation ownership remains with L395 and the motor/merge-train coordinator.

## Existing work and dependencies

- CUDApp main at 232332422bfdc31c8918085b50f13c1e18ab702e already has the native backend and the Omega submission slice; `motor/README.md` describes the remaining serving integration.
- aien-dev/omega-mv#618 (`opencuda/consume`, head 67c70741c8cec5c33e28a099d7c83bbd4f3ab839 when inspected) is OPEN/BLOCKED and pins CUDApp 8f0b645dbc859f1b63868cec77880621aa70b42d.
- Existing L395 evidence reports byte-identical archive/22-target host agreement. That is not proof the complete live serving artifact consumes the canonical backend.
- Extraction deletes GPU files modified by omega PRs #614..#617. Preserve/carry their existing changes before extraction, or port them into CUDApp and update the pin. Do not blindly reverse this technical dependency to imitate priority order. Prioritize the integration result, while preserving prerequisites.
- The already-deployed motor speed build (L387) is a separate milestone; it does not by itself prove canonical CUDApp consumption.

## Acceptance: MOTOR-CANONICAL-E2E

- [ ] Build from immutable CUDApp/Omega/sovereign-core source SHAs with an explicit CUDApp lock; no stale sibling checkout or silent fallback supplies GPU sources.
- [ ] Build/link provenance identifies the exact canonical GPU library and code path used by the serving binary; prove no divergent duplicate implementation is selected.
- [ ] Reuse the shared merge-train candidate/model load. Golden tokens match the reference, concurrent output equals alone, second turn works, and a real tool call parses. Include mutants that select a wrong pin/backend so the provenance check can fail.
- [ ] Publish binary/library hashes, lock contents, source SHAs, test commands and exact-commit public receipts. Prove no CUDA user-space libraries are mapped/imported in the serving path; do not confuse that with independence from NVIDIA's kernel driver.
- [ ] Only after that candidate passes, let the serving coordinator perform one safe swap with rollback and verify the running artifact/readiness. No restart/unload by this issue-filing pass.

Priority order after this: concurrency/recovery, general BF16/FP8 GEMM/reductions/scans, disassembler, independent-driver hardware qualification. Keep the experimental driver isolated from the working path until validated.


## Mandatory closure gate

Do not close from a branch push, a simulator-only result for a chip requirement, an agent summary, or a merged PR alone. Do not use auto-closing `Fixes`/`Closes` keywords in a PR until the full gate below is actually met.

- [ ] Link the full tested source SHA for every affected repository and the integrated/merged SHA. If a rebase, pin change, or merge changes executable inputs, qualify the resulting exact commit again.
- [ ] Link a committed public receipt and raw logs under `evidence/`: exact command and flags, compiler/tool and binary hashes, source/pin SHAs, machine/chip/driver identity, expected result and actual exit code.
- [ ] All acceptance checks pass; relevant negative controls/mutants fail for the intended reason. No skipped/waived gate or retry-until-green.
- [ ] Hardware rows have actual GB10 receipts in a coordinated chip window. Host/simulator tests remain separately identified and cannot satisfy those rows.
- [ ] Required dependencies are complete, independent review is recorded, and the integration owner verifies the receipt against the final artifact before closing this issue.

Existing implemented pieces must be reused, not rewritten. A historical draft is provenance, not proof that its host work is still missing. Live execution, pinned CUDApp consumption, and the independent driver remain distinct claims.

## Problem
Existing paged/GQA/split attention and shared-prefix staging do not by themselves prove shared-prefix reads are amortized across requests. Reuse those pieces and add composable attention states.

## Implementation
Represent immutable shared KV pages and per-request suffixes; batch distinct queries against the common prefix. Return output plus log-sum-exp (LSE) for each partition and merge with stable max-rescaled weights. Never reuse one request's attention output for a different query.

## Acceptance
- [ ] For two partitions, implement O=(exp(lp-m)*Op+exp(ls-m)*Os)/(exp(lp-m)+exp(ls-m)), m=max(lp,ls), and the corresponding merged LSE.
- [ ] Validate GQA head mapping, masks/positions, empty prefix/suffix, unequal suffixes, long contexts, page sharing/refcounts and extreme logits.
- [ ] Compare to unsplit attention under the declared numerical contract; mathematical exactness is not a bitwise guarantee.
- [ ] Mutants for missing LSE weighting, wrong head/page/position and stale shared pages fail.
- [ ] Measure prefix-read estimates, gather/merge overhead and end-to-end latency over supported batch sizes, prefix lengths and sharing ratios.
- [ ] Select the shared path only above measured break-even; preserve the ordinary attention path.

Research: Hydragen (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2402.05099) and FlashInfer (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2501.01005). Their original GPU gains are not GB10 predictions.

## Problem
Request lengths change during serving. Existing split decode, paged attention and reservations should be reused while assigning uneven attention work efficiently.

## Scope
Add a bounded plan containing per-CTA work, split/reduction maps, stable workspace addresses and explicit shape/capacity limits. Reuse plans across compatible layers. Keep serving admission and request policy in the model-serving consumer.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Plan and execute batches with heterogeneous query/KV lengths without padding all work to the longest request.
- [ ] Preserve fixed workspace capacities and detect overflow/stale plan/changed page table before submission.
- [ ] Reuse existing reservation/seal behavior; no hidden allocation during sealed execution.
- [ ] Document deterministic assignment and reduction order, with comparisons to the current attention path.
- [ ] Exercise empty requests, maximum limits, changed lengths, reused pages and plan-generation mutants.
- [ ] Benchmark CPU planning, plan upload, GPU execution and end-to-end latency separately; establish when cross-layer reuse amortizes planning.

Research: FlashInfer (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2501.01005), especially plan/run separation and deterministic ragged scheduling. Reimplement transferable mechanisms in the native stack; no CUDA JIT dependency in deployment.

## Problem
CUDApp owns IR, register allocation and scheduling controls. The host warp simulator executes IR, so passing it alone cannot prove emitted machine bytes or scheduling fields are correct.

## Dependencies and scope
Reuse #10's disassembler and existing fixtures/chip probes. Begin with legal basic-block reorderings in one measured hot kernel; preserve the current generator. Measure GB10 latency facts rather than copying A100 dependency tables.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Define a bounded candidate space and reject data, predicate, scoreboard, fixed-latency, branch/reconvergence, register-bundle and resource violations.
- [ ] Independently decode/check emitted instructions and controls, alongside IR simulation, reference outputs and repeated chip tests.
- [ ] Include malformed encoding, dependency and control-field mutants; a shared encoder/decoder assumption is not independent proof.
- [ ] Time candidates only after correctness passes; use paired repeated measurements, holdout shapes/inputs and explicit search budgets.
- [ ] Store candidate lineage, bytes/digest, target facts, resource use and validation/timing receipts.
- [ ] Freeze validated winners for reproducible deployment; retain the baseline when no robust improvement is demonstrated.

## Problem
src/omega_gpu_platform_linux.c checks MemAvailable before allocating, but separate processes can observe the same free budget. Unreadable memory information currently allows allocation. Extend #8's existing guard without replacing its tested behavior or claiming a system-wide OOM guarantee.

## Scope
Define explicit weight/intermediate/KV/marker usage, ownership, lifetime and cache/visibility rules. Add coordinated reservations for cooperating CUDApp processes using the existing isolation work from #6; account for external memory pressure separately.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Specify reserve/acquire/commit/release and process-death recovery; prevent two cooperating processes spending the same reservation.
- [ ] Check arithmetic overflow and invalid settings; define configurable behavior for missing/stale memory information.
- [ ] Preserve established uncached marker visibility and use cached weights only under the proven ownership contract.
- [ ] Host tests exercise simultaneous contenders, cancellation, crash cleanup, stale ownership and reservation-bypass mutants.
